summary: Every command ends with an exit code: 0 means success and any other number means failure. && and || use that code to decide whether to run the next command, and exit sets your script's own code.
notes: In the session, ./check-log.sh logs/server.log; echo "Exit code: $?" runs both commands on one line so $? is the script's code.
./check-log.sh logs/today.log && echo "Safe to archive" prints the message only because the script exited with 0.
{ echo ...; exit 2; } groups two commands so both run when the test fails. The spaces and the last ; are required.
pitfall: $? changes after every command, even echo. Save it right away (status=$?) if you need it more than once, or the second check reads echo's 0.
